questions.stem: The enzyme creatine kinase is normally found in the muscle cells. What does it mean if high levels of the enzyme are detected in the blood? Note: Be specific.

options.text: Production of the enzyme by the blood cells.

questions.answerRationale: Not starred, so this is our guess. Creatine kinase belongs inside muscle cells; finding it in the blood means muscle cells were damaged and leaked it (C). His text lists high creatine kinase as one way myositis is DETECTED, so B is the runner-up, but myositis is one cause of the damage, not what the finding means. 'Be specific' points away from D (activity) and E.
